Design ONE complete new front cover for the UK gardening book 'The Vegetable Guru', author John Lennon, portrait 185:240 proportions, approximately 1110 x 1440. This is a considered adult illustrated gardening-book cover. The user prefers our 'harvest on cream' concept over an earlier overly synthetic garden scene, and now wants to explore a different publisher-inspired composition. Make an art-directed, restrained graphic design: flat quiet background fields, controlled hierarchy, convincing simplified plant forms and useful open space.

REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is a downloaded PUBLISHED COVER used ONLY for its broad compositional ideas, pacing and organisation. Create original artwork, own title and a distinct layout; do not reproduce its publisher logo, author names, blurbs, exact drawings or other text. Images 2–4 are OUR APPROVED INTERIOR VEGETABLE HEROES: carrot, beetroot, French bean. Use them as the direct authority for drawing style. Crop illustrations must use broad overlapping colour planes, confident silhouettes, dimensional but simplified shading, a few graphic pale highlight slashes, forest/lime greens and recognisable crop colours. Keep the clean shape language, not the glowing dark/transparent preview backgrounds. No glow, halo, heavy black outline, glossy 3D rendering, elaborate fine botanical hatching, faces, toy-like vegetables or excessively intricate foliage. At the smaller cover scale use fewer well-chosen marks, with tidy irregularity and convincing leaf attachments. Image 5 is the actual LILITA ONE font specimen: match its letter shapes, modest natural roundness and weight. Use this one typeface for every text element, with different sizes for hierarchy. All text has flat ink colour: no extrusion, bevel, fake shadow or hand-drawn distortion.

Required exact words: 'The Vegetable Guru'; 'Your at-a-glance growing companion'; 'John Lennon'. Also retain a discreet small YouTube play symbol with 'As seen on YouTube' and '@hackriculture'. This feature is secondary, not large advertising. No guide count, extra badges, quotes or new copy. Lettering must be precise and complete, with comfortable trim margins. Keep the title dominant and readable at thumbnail scale, supporting words clearly secondary. This is a full flat cover image, no spine, no perspective, no photographed object, no grey studio backdrop and no multiple designs in one output.

CONCEPT C — STRUCTURED CROP GRID, inspired by the organisation of How to Grow Food in image 1. Use a warm clear sunny yellow field, forest-green typography and crisp thin forest-green rules. Build our own carefully proportioned practical handbook composition: a generous title area in the upper portion, with small 'The' and the words 'Vegetable' and 'Guru' on two main lines in Lilita One, followed by our complete subtitle in two smaller lines. A small YouTube feature can sit in the upper-right margin, balancing 'The'. Below the title, a disciplined three-column by two-row grid holds SIX SMALL ILLUSTRATIONS, with the same yellow field continuing through every cell. No differently coloured tiles or bulky shaded panels. A fine outer frame and a few dividers give an organised printed-almanac feel; use a quiet uncluttered footer for 'John Lennon'. Each tile has substantial breathing room and one crop only, scaled consistently: carrots with tops; a small red tomato truss; French bean pods; purple beetroot with leaves; onions/shallots; a leafy lettuce. Render all six in OUR hero language from images 2–4, including the related tomatoes/onions/lettuce, not the reference book's etched illustrations of hands, a watering can, jar or pan. Do not add plant labels or step numbers. Several crops may angle slightly, with full tips and leaves inside their cells; no illustrations crossing the grid or becoming giant. Make the grid and lettering feel balanced and deliberate, not a generic clip-art worksheet. No harvest heap, potting table, scenic background or pictorial garden. Bright, graphic, confident, orderly and genuinely useful-looking as a practical reference book.
